item.title: Cherry Angioma Removal: Cosmetic Vascular Lesion Treatment
item.dc:creator: Vijayan
item.content:encoded:
Cherry Angioma Removal: Your Treatment Options

Cherry angioma removal addresses benign, red moles (Campbell de Morgan spots) that appear with age. While harmless, they can be treated using methods like laser therapy, electrocautery, or shave excision. This guide compares these techniques, explains the recovery process, and clarifies why specialist care from a plastic surgeon is vital for achieving the best cosmetic outcome with minimal scarring, especially in delicate areas like the face. This ensures you make an informed choice about your care.

As a consultant plastic surgeon, Mr. Roshan Vijayan, FRCS (Plast), prioritises a collaborative approach to ensure your goals are understood and met. His extensive experience in both the NHS and private practice across London and Hertfordshire provides a reassuring standard of care. To explore your treatment options and discuss a bespoke solution, we invite you to Book Now a one-on-one consultation.

Table of Contents

  • What Are Cherry Angiomas (Red Moles)?
  • Why Do Cherry Angiomas Appear and Should I Be Concerned?
  • How Are Cherry Angiomas Removed?
  • Laser vs. Excision: Which Cherry Angioma Removal Is Best?
  • What Is the Recovery and Aftercare Process?
  • Why Choose a Plastic Surgeon for Your London Treatment?
  • Your Cherry Angioma Removal Consultation With Mr. Vijayan

What Are Cherry Angiomas (Red Moles)?

Cherry angioma removal is a common request, but understanding what these marks are is the first step. Also known as Campbell de Morgan spots or senile angiomas, cherry angiomas are benign vascular lesions. They are essentially small, harmless growths made up of clusters of dilated capillaries or tiny blood vessels at the surface of the skin. This collection of blood vessels is what gives them their characteristic bright, cherry-red colour.

These red moles typically present as small, smooth dots, often no bigger than a pinhead. They can be flat against the skin or become slightly raised and dome-shaped over time. Whilst they can appear anywhere on the body, they most frequently develop on the torso, shoulders, arms, and legs. It is also not uncommon to find them on the face and scalp.

The most important characteristic of a cherry angioma is that it is completely harmless. They are not cancerous, nor do they have the potential to become cancerous. They are a purely cosmetic concern for most people. However, any skin lesion that changes rapidly in size, shape, or colour, or begins to bleed without trauma, should always be evaluated by a medical professional to rule out other conditions. As a consultant plastic surgeon, part of my role is to provide an accurate diagnosis before considering any treatment for these or other benign skin lesions.

Why Do Cherry Angiomas Appear and Should I Be Concerned?

The precise cause of cherry angiomas is not fully understood, but their appearance is strongly linked to two primary factors: age and genetics. They tend to increase in number from the age of 30 onwards, and it is estimated that most adults will have at least a few by the time they reach their 70s. If your parents or other close family members have them, you are more likely to develop them as well, suggesting a clear genetic predisposition.

Beyond the natural ageing process, other factors may contribute to their development. Hormonal fluctuations, particularly those occurring during pregnancy, are often associated with an increase in their number and size. In some instances, exposure to certain chemicals or specific medical conditions can be a trigger, but for the vast majority of people, they are simply an inherited trait that becomes more prominent with age.

For patients, the key question is often: "Should I be concerned?" In almost all cases, the answer is no. These common blood spots are not an indicator of an underlying health problem. They do not require medical removal. The decision to proceed with treatment is almost always based on personal preference. Reasons for seeking removal include:

  • Cosmetic Appearance: Many people choose to remove them because they are unhappy with their appearance, especially when they are numerous or located on visible areas like the face, neck, or chest.
  • Irritation and Bleeding: A raised angioma located in an area of high friction—such as under a bra strap, along a waistband, or where jewellery sits—can be easily caught or scratched. This can cause them to bleed quite profusely due to their vascular nature. Removing them can prevent this repeated discomfort and inconvenience.

If you are considering removal for any of these reasons, a consultation can help determine the most appropriate course of action for your specific situation.

How Are Cherry Angiomas Removed?

Cherry angiomas are removed using precise techniques that target the blood vessels within the lesion, causing them to collapse and be reabsorbed by the body. The goal is to eliminate the red spot with minimal impact on the surrounding skin. The most effective methods are quick, performed in a clinical setting, and require little to no downtime.

The primary professional treatments for cherry angioma removal include:

  • Laser Removal: This is often the preferred method for smaller, flat angiomas, especially on the face and neck. A specialised vascular laser (such as a Pulsed Dye Laser or KTP laser) emits a specific wavelength of light that is selectively absorbed by the red pigment (haemoglobin) in the blood vessels. This energy heats and seals the vessels, causing the angioma to fade and disappear over a few weeks.
  • Electrocautery (Hyfrecation): This technique uses a fine-tipped probe to deliver a precise, low-level electrical current to the angioma. The heat from the current cauterises (burns) the blood vessels, effectively destroying the lesion. It is highly effective for both flat and slightly raised angiomas and offers excellent control for the practitioner.
  • Shave Excision: For larger, more prominent, or dome-shaped angiomas, a shave excision may be recommended. After numbing the area with a local anaesthetic, a surgical blade is used to carefully shave the lesion off, level with the surrounding skin. This method has the added benefit of providing a tissue sample that can be sent for histological analysis if there is any diagnostic uncertainty.
  • Cryotherapy: This involves applying liquid nitrogen to freeze the lesion. Whilst it can be effective, it is often less favoured for cherry angiomas as it offers less precision than laser or electrocautery and carries a slightly higher risk of causing pigmentary changes (lightening or darkening) in the surrounding skin.

Laser vs. Excision: Which Cherry Angioma Removal Is Best?

Choosing the right treatment method is crucial for achieving the best possible cosmetic outcome with the lowest risk. The decision between laser therapy and a surgical approach like shave excision depends on the specific characteristics of the angioma, its location, and the patient's goals. As a consultant plastic surgeon, my recommendation is always tailored to the individual. Here is a comparison to help you understand the key differences.

Best For

Laser Treatment is ideally suited for small to medium-sized, flat, or only slightly raised cherry angiomas. It is particularly effective for treating multiple lesions in one session and is the treatment of choice for cosmetically sensitive areas like the face, neck, and décolletage, where precision is paramount.

Shave Excision is generally reserved for larger, thicker, or significantly raised (dome-shaped) angiomas. It is also the most appropriate method if there is any doubt about the diagnosis, as the removed tissue can be examined under a microscope to confirm that it is benign.

Scarring Risk

Laser Treatment has a very low risk of scarring. Because the laser energy selectively targets the blood vessels without breaking the skin's surface, the surrounding tissue is largely unaffected. The most common after-effects are temporary redness or a small crust, which heals without leaving a mark in the vast majority of cases.

Shave Excision involves removing the lesion at the skin's surface, which will result in a small, flat wound. This typically heals to leave a minimal mark, often a small, flat circular scar that may be slightly paler than the surrounding skin. With the meticulous technique of a plastic surgeon, such as Mr. Roshan Vijayan, FRCS (Plast), this scar is typically very discreet and often less noticeable than the original angioma.

Procedure and Recovery

Both procedures are very quick, often taking just a few minutes per lesion. Laser treatment feels like a quick snap of an elastic band against the skin. Recovery involves the treated spot darkening and forming a tiny crust that falls off within one to two weeks. A shave excision is performed under local anaesthetic, so it is painless. It may require a small plaster or dressing for a few days, and the site will heal over a similar timeframe.

What Is the Recovery and Aftercare Process?

The recovery from cherry spots removal is typically straightforward and swift, with minimal disruption to your daily routine. Proper aftercare is essential to ensure the best possible cosmetic result and minimise any risk of complication, such as infection or changes in skin pigmentation.

Following your procedure, you can expect a predictable healing timeline. The treated area will initially appear slightly red or bruised. Within a day or two, a small, dark scab or crust will form over the site. This is a natural part of the healing process and acts as a protective barrier. It is crucial that you do not pick, scratch, or scrub this scab. You must allow it to fall off on its own, which usually happens within 7 to 14 days.

To support this process, your aftercare instructions will include:

  • Keeping the Area Clean: Gently clean the area with a mild cleanser and water, then pat it dry carefully. Avoid harsh soaps or scrubbing.
  • Applying Ointment: You may be advised to apply a thin layer of an antiseptic or petroleum-based ointment to keep the area moist and protected, which can aid healing and reduce crusting.
  • Sun Protection: Once the scab has fallen off, the new skin underneath will be sensitive. Protecting this area from the sun is paramount. You must apply a high-SPF (50+) broad-spectrum sunscreen daily for several months to prevent post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (darkening of the skin).
  • Avoiding Irritation: For a week or two, avoid swimming pools, saunas, and high-impact exercise that could cause excessive sweating or friction on the treated area.

A common question is, "Do they grow back?" The specific angioma that has been treated will not return. However, the treatment does not prevent the formation of new cherry angiomas elsewhere on the body, as the underlying predisposition to developing them remains.

Why Choose a Plastic Surgeon for Your London Treatment?

Whilst cherry angioma removal may seem like a minor procedure, the person performing it has a significant impact on both your safety and the final aesthetic outcome. In a landscape with many providers, from beauty therapists to GPs, choosing a board-certified Consultant Plastic Surgeon offers distinct advantages, particularly for a procedure where the primary goal is cosmetic improvement.

First and foremost is the matter of diagnosis. An experienced plastic surgeon, with years of training in the NHS and private practice, has the expertise to accurately diagnose skin lesions. This ensures that what is being treated is indeed a benign cherry angioma and not something that requires a different medical approach. This diagnostic certainty is the foundation of safe treatment.

Second is the focus on minimising scarring. A plastic surgeon’s entire training is centred on techniques that preserve tissue and create the most discreet scars possible. When performing an angioma treatment, especially with electrocautery or shave excision on a highly visible area like the face, this specialised skill is invaluable. As a Fellow of the Royal College of Surgeons in Plastic Surgery, FRCS (Plast), Mr. Vijayan applies a meticulous approach to every procedure, no matter how small, to ensure the resulting mark is minimal.

Finally, a surgeon has the full spectrum of treatment options available. They can expertly wield a laser, perform precise electrocautery, and, crucially, carry out a surgical excision if it is the best clinical choice. This versatility ensures that your treatment plan is not limited by the practitioner’s skillset but is genuinely tailored to what will give you the best result. For patients in London and Hertfordshire seeking the highest standard of care for cosmetic lesion removal, consulting with a qualified plastic surgeon is the most reliable path to a safe and aesthetically pleasing outcome.

Your Cherry Angioma Removal Consultation With Mr. Vijayan

Your journey towards clearer skin begins with a thorough and unhurried consultation. This is an opportunity for you to discuss your concerns and for Mr. Vijayan to provide a comprehensive assessment. He will carefully examine the lesion(s) you wish to have removed, confirm the diagnosis of cherry angioma, and talk through your aesthetic goals.

Based on the size, location, and type of angioma, Mr. Vijayan will explain the most suitable treatment options for you, detailing the procedure, the expected recovery, and the realistic outcomes. This collaborative discussion ensures you have all the information needed to make a confident and informed decision. The consultation is also when a clear, transparent cost for the proposed treatment will be provided.

To discuss your options with Mr. Vijayan, book a personal consultation at his practice serving patients across London, Hertfordshire, and Stevenage.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does cherry angioma removal cost?

The cost for private cherry angioma removal depends on the number, size, and location of the lesions, as well as the specific treatment method required. A precise quote is provided during your consultation after a full assessment of your skin.

In general, laser treatments may be priced per session, while an excision is priced per lesion. The consultation fee is typically separate from the final procedure cost.

Will the removal leave a scar?

The risk of noticeable scarring is very low, particularly with laser and electrocautery, which precisely target the lesion with minimal impact on surrounding skin. A shave excision for a larger angioma may leave a very small, fine line that typically fades well over time.

Mr. Vijayan employs meticulous surgical techniques focused on achieving the best possible cosmetic outcome.

How many treatments are needed to remove a cherry angioma?

Most small to medium-sized cherry angiomas are successfully and permanently removed in a single treatment session. Larger or more prominent lesions might occasionally require a second session to achieve complete clearance, which would be discussed with you beforehand.

Your expected treatment plan will be clearly outlined during your initial consultation.

Is cherry angioma removal painful?

The procedure involves minimal discomfort. Patients often describe the sensation from laser or electrocautery as a very brief, hot pinprick. For a shave excision, a local anaesthetic is always administered, meaning you will not feel any pain during the removal itself.

Any post-procedure tenderness is minor and resolves quickly.

Can I have multiple cherry angiomas removed in one session?

Yes, it is very common and efficient to treat multiple cherry angiomas in a single appointment. This is the preferred approach for many patients who have numerous small lesions on their torso, arms, or other areas of the body.

The total number that can be safely addressed in one session will be determined during your consultation.

Who should perform my cherry angioma removal?

For the safest procedure and best cosmetic results, removal should be performed by a qualified doctor, such as a consultant plastic surgeon or dermatologist. They can provide an accurate diagnosis, rule out other skin lesions, and select the most appropriate technique to minimise scarring.

This is especially important for lesions on visible areas like the face.

item.title: Breast Reduction Sleeping: Best Positions and Recovery Tips
item.dc:creator: Vijayan
item.content:encoded:
Breast Reduction Sleeping: Safe & Comfortable Recovery

Breast reduction sleeping requires careful management for a smooth recovery. This guide explains the best sleep positions, the use of pillows for support, and the timeline for returning to your usual habits. We also cover often-overlooked topics, such as how to prepare your bedroom environment before your procedure to aid your comfort and rest during the crucial early stages of healing, ensuring a more manageable recovery period.

This guidance is provided by Mr. Roshan Vijayan, FRCS (Plast), a Consultant Plastic Surgeon. As an NHS Consultant based in Stevenage, he also maintains a private practice for patients. To discuss your options with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, book a personal consultation at his practice serving patients across London, Hertfordshire, and Stevenage.

Table of Contents

  • Why is Your Sleep Position Important After Breast Reduction?
  • What is the Best Position for Sleeping After Breast Reduction?
  • How Can You Make Back-Sleeping More Comfortable?
  • What is the Timeline for Returning to Normal Sleep Positions?
  • Can Speciality Pillows Aid Your Breast Reduction Recovery?
  • How Should Hertfordshire Patients Prepare for Post-Surgery Sleep?
  • Realistic Outcomes: What to Expect from Your Sleep Recovery
  • Discuss Your Recovery With a Specialist Plastic Surgeon

Why is Your Sleep Position Important After Breast Reduction?

Your approach to breast reduction sleeping is a fundamental component of your recovery. Following a reduction mammoplasty procedure, your body needs rest to heal effectively, and your sleeping position directly influences swelling, comfort, and the integrity of your surgical results. Adopting the correct posture at night protects the delicate healing tissues from undue strain and pressure.

Sleeping in a recommended position helps to manage postoperative swelling by promoting proper fluid drainage. It also minimises the risk of putting accidental pressure on your incisions, which is essential for neat scar formation and preventing complications such as wound separation (dehiscence). An incorrect sleeping posture, particularly on your front or side, can pull on the sutures, increase discomfort, and potentially compromise the final aesthetic outcome of your breast reduction surgery. By consciously managing how you sleep, you take an active role in safeguarding your health and your surgical investment, ensuring a smoother and more comfortable healing journey.

What is the Best Position for Sleeping After Breast Reduction?

The optimal breast reduction sleep position is on your back with your head and upper body elevated. This posture, known as the supine position, is universally recommended by plastic surgeons for several key reasons. Firstly, it prevents any direct pressure on your newly contoured breasts, which are sensitive and require protection as they heal. Lying on your back ensures that gravity is distributed evenly across your body, avoiding targeted strain on the chest area and incision lines.

Secondly, elevation is a critical factor. Propping your torso up to a 30-45 degree angle with pillows or a wedge helps to significantly reduce postoperative swelling and bruising. This slight incline assists with fluid dynamics, encouraging excess fluid to move away from the surgical site, which in turn can alleviate feelings of tightness and discomfort. It can also make breathing feel easier in the initial days following the procedure.

Consistently wearing your provided surgical or compression bra, even while you sleep, is non-negotiable. This garment provides essential support, stabilises the breast tissue, minimises movement, and helps to control swelling. Sleeping on your back, elevated, and in your surgical bra creates the ideal environment for your body to recover efficiently and safely. While it may be an adjustment for those accustomed to sleeping on their side or front, committing to this position for the initial recovery period is one of the most important contributions you can make to your healing.

How Can You Make Back-Sleeping More Comfortable?

For many individuals, transitioning to back-sleeping is one of the most challenging aspects of recovery. However, with some preparation, you can create a comfortable and supportive environment that promotes restful sleep. The key is to build a 'nest' that supports your entire body, not just your back.

Start by placing a firm pillow or wedge behind your head and shoulders to achieve the necessary elevation. To prevent you from rolling onto your side during the night, place firm pillows on either side of your torso, tucking them in snugly from your armpits to your hips. This creates a gentle barrier that provides a sense of security and stability. Placing another pillow under your knees is also highly beneficial; this small adjustment alleviates pressure on your lower back, a common point of discomfort for new back-sleepers, and helps to maintain a comfortable spinal alignment.

Beyond physical supports, consider your overall sleep hygiene. Take your prescribed pain medication approximately 30-60 minutes before you intend to sleep, allowing it to take effect. Establish a calming pre-sleep routine, such as reading a book, listening to a podcast, or practising gentle breathing exercises. Avoid screen time in the hour before bed, as blue light can disrupt your natural sleep cycle. The psychological impact of disrupted sleep can be significant, so acknowledging that this is a temporary adjustment and focusing on creating a peaceful, comfortable sanctuary can make the process feel much more manageable.

What is the Timeline for Returning to Normal Sleep Positions?

Patience is paramount when it comes to resuming your preferred sleeping position. The timeline for returning to side or stomach sleeping varies between individuals and depends on your personal healing rate. The guidance provided by your surgeon should always be your primary reference, as it is tailored to your specific procedure. However, a general timeline can help manage your expectations.

  • Weeks 1-3: During this initial and most critical healing phase, sleeping on your back in an elevated position is mandatory. There should be no exceptions. This position protects your incisions, controls swelling, and allows the breast tissues to settle without external pressure. Attempting to sleep on your side or front during this time poses a significant risk to your surgical outcome.
  • Weeks 4-6: As you progress in your recovery timeline, and with your surgeon's clearance, you may be able to begin transitioning. Some patients find they can start sleeping on their side for short periods. It is advisable to use pillows to support your back and breasts to prevent you from rolling completely onto your front. Listen to your body; if you experience any pain or discomfort, return to sleeping on your back. Sleeping on your stomach is still strongly discouraged.
  • After 6-8 Weeks: Most patients receive approval from their surgeon to resume sleeping in any position they find comfortable, including on their stomach. By this stage, the initial healing is well-established, and the internal structures are more robust. However, you may still experience some residual tenderness, so a gradual reintroduction to your normal sleeping habits is the most sensible approach.

This timeline is a guide. Your personal recovery is unique, and Mr. Roshan Vijayan provides specific, individualised advice for each of his patients based on their progress during follow-up appointments.

Can Speciality Pillows Aid Your Breast Reduction Recovery?

While not strictly necessary, many patients find that a speciality breast reduction pillow or a strategic pillow arrangement can make a substantial difference to their comfort and sleep quality. These pillows are designed to provide targeted support, making it easier to maintain the recommended back-sleeping position throughout the night.

Several types of pillows can be beneficial:

  • Wedge Pillow: This is perhaps the most useful investment. A foam wedge provides consistent and stable elevation for your upper body, which is often more reliable than a stack of regular pillows that can shift during the night. They are available in various angles, with 30-45 degrees being ideal for post-surgical recovery.
  • Pregnancy or U-Shaped Pillow: These large, full-body pillows are excellent for creating a supportive 'nest'. They wrap around your body, providing support for your back, neck, and hips simultaneously. The 'arms' of the pillow also act as effective barriers, making it very difficult to roll onto your side unconsciously while asleep.
  • Mastectomy or Chest Pillow: While often associated with mastectomy recovery, these soft, contoured pillows can be useful during the day. They are designed to be placed under the arms and across the chest to protect the area from accidental bumps, the pressure of a seatbelt, or even a pet jumping on your lap. They are not typically used for sleeping but can enhance comfort while resting.

You do not need to purchase all these items. Often, a combination of a good wedge and several firm standard pillows to support your sides and knees is entirely sufficient. The goal is to create a system that feels secure and comfortable for you.

How Should Hertfordshire Patients Prepare for Post-Surgery Sleep?

For patients across London, Stevenage, and Hertfordshire, preparing your home for post breast reduction sleeping before your surgery day can profoundly impact your comfort and peace of mind. A well-prepared recovery space allows you to focus solely on resting and healing. Think of it as creating a 'recovery hub' centred around your bed.

Your first step is to build your sleeping nest. Arrange your wedge and support pillows on your bed to test the setup. Make sure it feels comfortable and secure. Next, organise your bedside table so that everything you might need during the night is within easy reach. This includes:

  • A large bottle of water with a straw
  • Your prescribed medications and a schedule to track them
  • Your mobile phone and a long charging cable
  • Lip balm and a gentle moisturiser
  • Healthy, easy-to-eat snacks like crackers or a protein bar
  • The television remote or a book

This simple act of preparation prevents you from having to twist, stretch, or get out of bed unnecessarily, which can be difficult and uncomfortable in the first few days. Ensure the path from your bed to the bathroom is clear of any trip hazards. Fresh, clean bedding can also make your recovery space feel more comfortable and inviting. By taking these practical steps before your procedure, you create a calm, organised, and safe environment that is conducive to a smooth recovery.

Realistic Outcomes: What to Expect from Your Sleep Recovery

Undergoing breast reduction surgery is a significant decision, and understanding what to expect from your breast reduction recovery sleep is a vital part of the process. It is realistic to anticipate some level of sleep disruption in the first one to two weeks. Your body is healing, you may experience discomfort, and you are adapting to a new, unfamiliar sleeping position. This is a normal and temporary phase of recovery.

What can be achieved through diligent post-operative sleep care is a smoother, quicker, and more comfortable healing process. By sleeping on your back and elevated, you can actively minimise swelling, reduce strain on your incisions, and lower the risk of complications. This discipline supports the excellent surgical work performed and helps you achieve the best possible aesthetic result. Over the first few weeks, as your body heals and you become more accustomed to the position, your sleep quality will steadily improve.

What cannot be expected is an immediate return to your normal sleep patterns. It is not realistic to think you will be able to sleep on your side or stomach in the first month without consequence. Attempting to do so can compromise your results. As a Consultant Plastic Surgeon, Mr. Roshan Vijayan, FRCS (Plast), provides care grounded in the same high standards seen in his NHS work, prioritising patient safety and realistic expectations. The temporary adjustment in your sleeping habits is a short-term investment for a long-term, positive outcome.

Discuss Your Recovery With a Specialist Plastic Surgeon

Your recovery journey is as personal as your reasons for considering surgery. While this guide provides a general framework, your specific needs and healing progress will dictate your post-operative care. Having a clear, open dialogue with a specialist is essential to feeling confident and prepared for the recovery period. A dedicated consultation allows you to ask detailed questions and receive advice tailored specifically to you.

Mr. Roshan Vijayan is a Consultant Plastic Surgeon, FRCS (Plast), who believes in providing comprehensive, patient-centred care from the initial discussion through to the final stages of recovery. He ensures every patient understands the practical steps, like sleep positioning, that are crucial for a successful outcome.

To discuss your options with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, book a personal consultation at his practice serving patients across London, Hertfordshire, and Stevenage.

Frequently Asked Questions About Sleeping After Breast Reduction

How can I manage pain at night to sleep better after breast reduction?

Following the prescribed pain relief schedule is essential. Taking your medication approximately 30-60 minutes before you intend to sleep can help manage discomfort as you settle. Ensuring your supportive pillows are correctly positioned to prevent strain on your chest and upper body also contributes significantly to a more restful night.

Do I need to wear my surgical bra to bed?

Yes, you will be required to wear your surgical or compression garment continuously, including while sleeping, for the initial recovery period. This garment provides crucial support, minimises swelling, and helps protect your incisions as they heal. It is especially important at night when you cannot consciously control your movements.

Mr. Vijayan will provide specific instructions on the duration for which this is necessary.

Will sleeping in the wrong position compromise my surgical results?

While briefly rolling over is unlikely to cause lasting harm, consistently sleeping on your side or stomach too early in your recovery should be avoided. Doing so can increase swelling, place unnecessary tension on your healing suture lines, and may negatively affect the final aesthetic outcome of the procedure.

Is it normal to feel anxious or frustrated about sleep after surgery?

It is very common to experience some sleep disruption and associated frustration after any major surgery. The combination of physical discomfort, restricted movement, and a change in your normal routine can have a psychological impact. Acknowledging this as a temporary part of the recovery process can be helpful.

If these feelings persist, you should discuss them at your follow-up appointment.

Can I take sleeping aids after my breast reduction?

You must not take any over-the-counter sleeping tablets or herbal remedies without first consulting your surgical team. These substances can interfere with your prescribed pain medication or the lingering effects of anaesthesia. Your surgeon can advise on safe options if sleep becomes a significant concern during your recovery.

item.title: Pyogenic Granuloma Excision: Fast-Growing Lesion Treatment
item.dc:creator: Vijayan
item.content:encoded:
Pyogenic Granuloma Excision: A Patient's Overview

Pyogenic granuloma excision is a standard treatment for these benign skin lesions, which are known for bleeding easily. This guide details what a pyogenic granuloma is, the causes of frequent bleeding, and the various treatment options. We will offer a detailed comparison of removal techniques with a focus on cosmetic outcomes, a week-by-week recovery timeline, and specialist advice on how to manage any resulting scars, providing a comprehensive resource for your consideration.

Mr. Roshan Vijayan is a Consultant Plastic Surgeon, FRCS (Plast), who brings his expertise from his NHS consultant post in Stevenage to his private practice. To discuss your options with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, book a personal consultation at his practice serving patients across London, Hertfordshire, and Stevenage.

Table of Contents

  • What Is a Pyogenic Granuloma?
  • Why Do These Lesions Bleed So Easily?
  • Is Pyogenic Granuloma Excision Right for Me?
  • Are There Non-Surgical Granuloma Treatments?
  • The Pyogenic Granuloma Removal Procedure Explained
  • What Is Recovery Like After Granuloma Removal in London?
  • Realistic Outcomes and Managing Recurrence
  • Your Consultation with Mr. Roshan Vijayan

What Is a Pyogenic Granuloma?

A pyogenic granuloma, also known as a lobular capillary haemangioma, is a common and entirely benign (non-cancerous) skin growth. It is composed of a dense proliferation of small blood vessels, which gives it a characteristic bright red, raspberry-like appearance and causes it to bleed very easily with minor contact.

Despite their name, these lesions are neither "pyogenic" (pus-forming) nor true "granulomas" in a pathological sense. They are vascular growths that can appear suddenly and grow rapidly over a few weeks, often following a minor injury to the skin, though many occur without any identifiable trigger. They are most frequently found on the fingers, hands, face, head, and neck. While they can affect anyone at any age, they are more common in children, young adults, and during pregnancy due to hormonal changes. Although a pyogenic granuloma is not dangerous, its tendency to bleed and its appearance can be a significant nuisance. A definitive diagnosis from a specialist is important to distinguish it from other skin lesions.

Why Do These Lesions Bleed So Easily?

The primary reason pyogenic granulomas bleed so profusely with minimal provocation lies in their structure. These lesions are essentially an overgrowth of capillaries—the body's smallest blood vessels—clustered together in a fragile arrangement. This dense network of vessels is covered by only a very thin and delicate layer of skin (epithelium), which offers little protection. Consequently, any slight friction or minor trauma, such as brushing against clothing, towelling off after a shower, or an accidental knock, can easily rupture these surface-level capillaries.

When these vessels break, the bleeding can be surprisingly brisk and persistent for such a small lesion. This is the most common symptom that prompts individuals to seek medical advice and treatment. The constant cycle of bleeding, scabbing, and then bleeding again upon the slightest touch can be inconvenient, distressing, and disruptive to daily life. While the exact cause for their development is not always clear, factors such as physical trauma, hormonal fluctuations, and certain medications can trigger their growth. Understanding this vascular composition is key to appreciating why options like vascular lesion surgery are designed to remove the lesion completely at its base to prevent further bleeding episodes.

Is Pyogenic Granuloma Excision Right for Me?

Deciding if pyogenic granuloma excision is the most suitable course of action for you is a clinical decision made in consultation with a specialist surgeon. This procedure is generally recommended for individuals whose lesion causes significant problems, such as frequent and troublesome bleeding that interferes with daily activities. If the granuloma is located in a prominent or cosmetically sensitive area, such as the face or hands, removal may be desired for aesthetic reasons. Furthermore, if a lesion is easily irritated by clothing or daily tasks, leading to discomfort and repeated trauma, excision offers a definitive solution.

Another important reason for considering excision is diagnostic certainty. While a pyogenic granuloma has a typical appearance, it can occasionally mimic more serious skin conditions. Removing the lesion and sending it for histopathological analysis (examination under a microscope) provides a conclusive diagnosis and peace of mind. Candidacy for the procedure also depends on your general health and personal preferences. During a comprehensive consultation, a surgeon will assess the lesion, confirm the likely diagnosis, and discuss the benefits and risks of excision compared to other treatment options, helping you make an informed decision that aligns with your specific circumstances and treatment goals.

Are There Non-Surgical Granuloma Treatments?

While surgical excision is often considered the most definitive treatment, several non-surgical or minimally invasive alternatives exist for managing pyogenic granulomas. The suitability of these options depends on the size, location, and nature of the lesion, as well as patient factors. One common method is chemical cauterisation using silver nitrate, which can be applied topically to burn the lesion. However, this may require multiple applications and is often better suited for smaller, flatter granulomas.

Another approach is curettage and electrocautery. This involves scraping the lesion off with a spoon-shaped instrument (a curette) and then using a heated electrical probe to seal the blood vessels at the base. This method is quick and effective for many lesions but carries a higher rate of recurrence compared to full excision. Laser therapy, particularly with a pulse dye laser, can also be used. The laser targets the blood vessels within the granuloma, causing them to shrink and the lesion to fade. This can be an effective option, especially for lesions on the face, but may require several treatment sessions. It is important to recognise that these non-surgical methods, while less invasive, can have higher recurrence rates because they may not remove the "feeder" vessels at the very base of the lesion as reliably as a formal excision.

The Pyogenic Granuloma Removal Procedure Explained

The pyogenic granuloma excision is a straightforward and effective procedure, typically performed under local anaesthetic in a clinical setting. This means you will be awake, but the area around the lesion will be completely numb, ensuring you feel no discomfort during the removal. The process begins with a careful cleaning of the skin. Once the anaesthetic has taken effect, Mr. Vijayan will proceed with one of two primary techniques for the granuloma excision procedure.

Surgical Techniques

The choice of technique depends on the lesion's size, location, and the desired balance between recurrence risk and cosmetic outcome.

  • Curettage and Cautery: This involves using a specialised instrument called a curette to gently scrape the lesion from the skin's surface. The base is then treated with electrocautery (a gentle electrical current) to seal the underlying blood vessels. This technique is swift and does not require stitches, often resulting in a small, flat, circular scar. However, the risk of the granuloma returning is higher than with full excision.
  • Full-Thickness Excision: For a lower recurrence rate and often a more refined cosmetic result, a full-thickness excision is preferred. Mr. Roshan Vijayan, FRCS (Plast), uses his plastic surgery expertise to remove the entire lesion, including its base, within a small ellipse of skin. This approach is meticulous and mirrors similar excision techniques for benign lesions. The wound is then closed with very fine stitches, which helps to create a neat, linear scar that typically heals discreetly.

Regardless of the method used for the pyogenic granuloma removal, the removed tissue is always sent for histological analysis to confirm that it is benign. This step is a crucial part of the comprehensive care provided. Mr. Vijayan's experience in the surgical removal of skin lesions ensures the procedure is carried out with precision, focusing on both complete removal and an optimal aesthetic outcome.

What Is Recovery Like After Granuloma Removal in London?

Recovery following a pyogenic granuloma removal is generally quick and straightforward. As the procedure is performed under local anaesthetic, you can return home the same day. Immediately after the treatment, a protective dressing will be applied to the site, which you will be advised on how to care for.

Week-by-Week Expectations

  • First 24-48 Hours: The local anaesthetic will wear off within a few hours. Any mild discomfort is typically well managed with over-the-counter pain relief such as paracetamol. It is advisable to keep the area dry and avoid any strenuous activity that might stretch the skin or put pressure on the wound.
  • Week 1: You will be given instructions on when to change or remove the dressing. If stitches were used, they will remain in place. The area might appear slightly red, swollen, or bruised, which is a normal part of the healing process.
  • Week 2: If you had stitches, they are usually removed between 7 and 14 days after the procedure, depending on the location of the lesion and the rate of healing. Once the stitches are out, the initial wound healing is complete.
  • Following Months: The resulting scar will initially be pink or red. Over the next 6 to 12 months, it will gradually mature, fading in colour and becoming softer and flatter. Protecting the new scar from direct sun exposure is essential during this period to prevent it from becoming permanently darkened.

Following the specific aftercare advice provided by Mr. Vijayan’s team is key to ensuring a smooth recovery and achieving the best possible cosmetic result.

Realistic Outcomes and Managing Recurrence

The primary goals of treatment for a pyogenic granuloma are to stop the bleeding, remove the cosmetically bothersome lesion, and obtain a definitive diagnosis. Surgical excision successfully achieves these aims in the vast majority of cases. However, it is important to have realistic expectations about the aesthetic outcome. Any procedure that cuts through the full thickness of the skin will result in a permanent scar. As a Consultant Plastic Surgeon, Mr. Vijayan uses specialised techniques to place incisions and use fine sutures to ensure the resulting scar is as neat and inconspicuous as possible. Over time, most scars fade to a fine line that is not easily noticeable.

Recurrence is a known possibility with pyogenic granulomas, as they can regrow if any microscopic vascular tissue is left behind. The risk of this happening is directly related to the removal technique. Full-thickness excision, which removes the lesion at its base, has a very low recurrence rate, typically below 5%. In contrast, less invasive methods like curettage or topical treatments have a higher chance of recurrence, sometimes reported as high as 40%. Should a lesion recur, it can be treated again, usually with a formal excision to ensure complete removal.

Effective post-procedure care is vital for an optimal outcome. This includes proper wound care in the initial weeks and long-term scar management. Simple measures like massaging the scar, using silicone-based gels, and diligent sun protection can significantly improve its final appearance. For any scars that remain prominent or concerning, there are advanced scar management strategies that can be discussed.

Your Consultation with Mr. Roshan Vijayan

Your journey begins with a private consultation with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, an experienced FRCS (Plast) accredited Consultant Plastic Surgeon. With a substantive NHS Consultant post in Stevenage, he brings a wealth of experience to his private practice. This initial meeting is a crucial step, providing you with the opportunity to receive an accurate diagnosis and a clear understanding of your condition. Mr. Vijayan will assess your lesion, discuss your symptoms, and explain the most appropriate treatment options in detail, ensuring all your questions are answered thoroughly and empathetically. This allows you to make a fully informed choice about your care.

To discuss your options with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, book a personal consultation at his practice serving patients across London, Hertfordshire, and Stevenage.

Frequently Asked Questions About Granuloma Treatment

Is a pyogenic granuloma dangerous?

A pyogenic granuloma is a benign (non-cancerous) skin growth and is not dangerous. However, its tendency to bleed easily with minor contact can be a significant nuisance. Removal is often recommended for comfort and to allow for histological analysis to confirm the diagnosis definitively.

Will pyogenic granuloma removal leave a scar?

Any procedure that involves an incision through the skin's full thickness, such as surgical excision, will result in a scar. As a plastic surgeon, Mr. Vijayan uses meticulous techniques to align the incision with natural skin lines and close the wound, aiming for the finest and least conspicuous scar possible.

Is pyogenic granuloma excision painful?

The procedure itself is performed under local anaesthetic, which numbs the area to prevent any pain during the removal. You may feel a brief stinging sensation as the anaesthetic is administered. Post-procedural discomfort is typically mild and can be managed effectively with standard pain relief medication.

How long does recovery take after granuloma excision?

Initial wound healing generally takes one to two weeks, during which you will have specific care instructions to follow. The scar will continue to mature and fade over many months. Most patients can return to their usual daily activities within a day or so, though strenuous exercise should be avoided initially.

What are the risks associated with the procedure?

As with any surgical procedure, excision carries small risks including bleeding, infection, and adverse scarring. There is also a small possibility that the granuloma may recur. Mr. Vijayan will discuss these potential outcomes with you in detail during your personal consultation.

How much does pyogenic granuloma excision cost?

The cost is determined by factors such as the lesion's size and location, the complexity of the procedure, and the chosen clinical facility. A precise and fully itemised quote will be provided to you following your initial consultation, once Mr. Vijayan has completed a thorough assessment of your case.

item.title: Extended Abdominoplasty: When Standard Tummy Tuck Isn't Enough
item.dc:creator: Vijayan
item.content:encoded:
Extended Abdominoplasty: Comprehensive Body Contouring

An extended abdominoplasty is a surgical procedure designed for comprehensive midsection contouring. This guide details how it differs from a standard tummy tuck, who is a suitable candidate, and what the recovery involves. We will also explore the limitations of non-surgical alternatives and provide a clear outline of what this procedure can and cannot realistically achieve, allowing you to make a fully informed decision about your options for addressing excess skin and fat.

Mr. Roshan Vijayan, FRCS (Plast), is a Consultant Plastic Surgeon with extensive experience in body contouring. He maintains a substantive NHS Consultant post based in Stevenage. To discuss your options with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, book a personal consultation at his practice serving patients across London, Hertfordshire, and Stevenage.

Table of Contents

  • What is an Extended Abdominoplasty?
  • How Does an Extended Tummy Tuck Differ from a Standard One?
  • Are You a Suitable Candidate for an Extended Tummy Tuck?
  • Exploring Non-Surgical Alternatives for Flank Contouring
  • The Extended Abdominoplasty Procedure: A Step-by-Step Overview
  • What Can You Expect During Your Recovery in Hertfordshire?
  • Realistic Outcomes: What an Extended Abdominoplasty Can Achieve
  • Discuss Your Contouring Goals with a Specialist Surgeon in London

What is an Extended Abdominoplasty?

An Extended Abdominoplasty is a comprehensive surgical procedure designed to remove a significant amount of excess skin and fat from the abdomen, flanks, and lower back. It is more extensive than a standard tummy tuck, addressing the entire circumference of the lower torso to create a smoother, more defined contour.

This procedure is particularly effective for individuals who have experienced massive weight loss, either through diet and exercise or bariatric surgery, and are left with substantial skin laxity that extends beyond the front of the abdomen. The primary goals are to tighten the underlying abdominal muscles, remove redundant skin that can cause discomfort and rashes, and improve the overall shape of the midsection. Unlike weight loss surgery, an extended abdominoplasty is a body contouring procedure. It refines the results of your weight loss efforts by addressing the tissue laxity that remains, helping to restore a firmer and more proportionate body shape. The technique involves a longer incision than a standard tummy tuck, allowing the surgeon to address the "love handles" and reshape the waistline more completely.

How Does an Extended Tummy Tuck Differ from a Standard One?

While both an extended tummy tuck and a standard abdominoplasty aim to create a flatter, more toned abdomen, their scope and surgical approach differ significantly. The primary distinction lies in the length of the incision and the areas of the body that are treated, making the extended version a more comprehensive option for specific patient needs.

A standard abdominoplasty typically involves an incision that runs from hip to hip, remaining low on the abdomen, often within the bikini line. This approach is highly effective for removing excess skin and fat and repairing separated muscles (diastasis recti) confined to the front of the abdomen. It is well-suited for patients whose concerns are primarily located between their hip bones.

In contrast, the extended tummy tuck utilises a longer incision that continues past the hip bones and around towards the lower back. This extended reach allows the surgeon to address concerns that wrap around the body. Key differences include:

  • Incision Length: The incision for an extended tummy tuck is significantly longer, enabling greater access to the flanks and back.
  • Areas Treated: A standard procedure focuses on the anterior abdomen. The extended procedure treats the abdomen, flanks (love handles), and can improve the contour of the upper buttocks and lower back by removing loose tissue.
  • Candidate Profile: Patients who have undergone substantial weight loss often have circumferential skin laxity, making them more suitable candidates for an extended procedure, whereas those with concerns limited to the front of the abdomen may only require a standard tummy tuck.

The choice between these procedures depends entirely on your individual anatomy and the extent of tissue laxity. A thorough consultation is essential to determine which approach will best achieve your desired aesthetic outcome.

Are You a Suitable Candidate for an Extended Tummy Tuck?

An extended tummy tuck is a significant surgical undertaking, and suitability is determined by a combination of physical factors, health status, and realistic expectations. This procedure is most beneficial for a specific group of individuals who find that diet and exercise alone cannot address the extensive skin laxity affecting their midsection.

Ideal candidates for this procedure generally share the following characteristics:

  • Significant Skin Laxity: You have a large amount of loose, sagging skin not only on your abdomen but also extending around your sides to your flanks and lower back. This is a common concern for patients after losing a substantial amount of weight or after multiple pregnancies.
  • Stable Weight: You are at or near your goal weight and have maintained it for at least six months. This stability is crucial as further significant weight fluctuations can compromise the surgical results.
  • Good General Health: You are in good physical health with no medical conditions that could impair healing or increase surgical risk. Being a non-smoker is vital, as smoking severely compromises blood flow and the healing process.
  • Realistic Expectations: You understand the scope of the procedure, the recovery process, and the nature of the resulting scar. You are seeking improvement in your body contour, not perfection.

This procedure is frequently considered by post-bariatric patients or women who find that their body has not returned to its pre-pregnancy state. For some, it is performed as part of a mummy makeover to address comprehensive changes to the torso. A personal consultation will allow for a full assessment of your anatomy and a discussion of whether this powerful contouring procedure aligns with your personal and aesthetic goals.

Exploring Non-Surgical Alternatives for Flank Contouring

In the field of aesthetics, various non-surgical treatments have emerged for body contouring. While these can be effective for certain individuals with specific concerns, it is crucial to understand their capabilities and limitations, particularly when compared to a surgical procedure like an extended abdominoplasty. Non-invasive options for flank contouring primarily focus on reducing small, localised pockets of fat.

Technologies such as cryolipolysis (fat freezing) and radiofrequency devices work by targeting and destroying fat cells, which are then naturally eliminated by the body over several weeks or months. These treatments can be appealing due to the lack of incisions, anaesthesia, and significant downtime. They may offer a modest improvement in contour for individuals who are already near their ideal weight and have good skin elasticity but are bothered by stubborn fat on their flanks or abdomen.

However, the limitations of these non-surgical methods are significant for candidates considering an extended abdominoplasty. Their primary and most critical limitation is that they do not address excess skin or muscle laxity. For a patient with significant skin redundancy following massive weight loss, simply reducing the underlying fat will not tighten the loose, overhanging skin. In some cases, it can even make the skin laxity appear more pronounced. Furthermore, non-surgical methods cannot repair separated abdominal muscles (diastasis recti). Therefore, for individuals with substantial skin and muscle concerns, these alternatives are generally not suitable and will not produce results comparable to surgical excision and repair.

The Extended Abdominoplasty Procedure: A Step-by-Step Overview

The Extended Abdominoplasty procedure is a carefully planned surgical sequence designed for comprehensive torso reshaping. Mr. Roshan Vijayan's approach is tailored to each patient's unique anatomy, focusing on safety and achieving a natural-looking, refined contour. The surgery is performed under general anaesthesia and typically takes several hours to complete.

The procedure generally involves the following key stages:

  1. Incision Placement: A horizontal incision is made low on the abdomen, similar to a standard tummy tuck but extending further around the hips towards the lower back. This allows for broad access to the entire lower torso. A second incision is carefully made around the umbilicus (navel) to free it from the surrounding skin.
  2. Tissue Elevation and Muscle Repair: The skin and underlying fat are lifted off the abdominal wall, exposing the abdominal muscles. If these muscles have become separated or weakened (a condition known as diastasis recti), they are repaired by being pulled back to the midline and tightened with strong internal sutures. This repair creates a firmer abdominal wall and a narrower waistline.
  3. Contouring and Fat Removal: To achieve the best possible shape, liposuction for optimal contouring is frequently used in conjunction with the procedure. This helps to remove residual fat deposits from the abdomen, hips, and flanks, further enhancing the final silhouette.
  4. Skin Excision and Repositioning: The elevated skin flap is then drawn down over the newly tightened abdomen. The excess skin and fat are precisely measured and surgically removed. A new opening is created for the navel, which is brought through and sutured into its new, natural position.
  5. Closure: The long incision is meticulously closed in layers to minimise tension and promote optimal scarring. Surgical drains may be placed beneath the skin to prevent fluid accumulation during the initial recovery period. A sterile dressing and a compression garment are applied.

What Can You Expect During Your Recovery in Hertfordshire?

Recovery from an extended abdominoplasty is a gradual process that requires patience and strict adherence to post-operative guidelines. Understanding the timeline and expectations is key to a smooth and successful outcome. As an experienced NHS Consultant, Mr. Vijayan prioritises patient safety and provides comprehensive support throughout the recovery journey.

Immediately following surgery, you can expect to stay in the hospital for one to three nights for monitoring. You will have surgical drains in place and will be fitted with a medical-grade compression garment to minimise swelling and support the healing tissues. Discomfort and tightness are normal and will be managed with prescribed pain medication.

The first two weeks are the most critical phase. Your mobility will be limited, and you will need to walk with a slight bend at the waist to avoid straining the incision line. Swelling and bruising will be at their peak during this time. It is essential to have assistance at home for daily tasks. Most patients can return to a desk-based job and light activities after two to four weeks. Strenuous exercise, heavy lifting, and intense physical activity must be avoided for at least six to eight weeks. The compression garment is typically worn for several weeks. Swelling can persist for many months, with the final results becoming apparent at around the six to twelve-month mark. Detailed post-operative care instructions will be provided. While the procedure has a high satisfaction rate, potential risks include infection, seroma (fluid collection), haematoma (bleeding), and issues with wound healing or scarring. These risks are uncommon and are minimised through careful surgical technique and post-operative management, but they will be discussed thoroughly during your consultation.

Realistic Outcomes: What an Extended Abdominoplasty Can Achieve

Setting realistic expectations is a cornerstone of patient satisfaction in plastic surgery. An Extended Abdominoplasty is a powerful procedure for body contouring, but it is important to have a clear understanding of what it can and cannot accomplish. During your consultation, Mr. Roshan Vijayan, FRCS (Plast), will provide a candid assessment of the results you can anticipate based on your specific anatomy and goals.

What the Procedure Can Achieve:

  • Removal of Excess Skin: The primary benefit is the removal of a significant amount of loose, sagging skin and stubborn fat from the front of the abdomen, the flanks, and the lower back.
  • Muscle Tightening: It effectively repairs diastasis recti (separation of the abdominal muscles), creating a flatter abdominal profile and a stronger core.
  • Improved Body Contour: The procedure creates a dramatically smoother, firmer, and more proportional contour around the entire midsection, often resulting in a more defined waistline.
  • Enhanced Comfort and Confidence: By removing excess skin, it can alleviate physical discomforts like chafing and rashes, and many patients report a substantial boost in self-esteem and find that clothes fit much better.

What the Procedure Cannot Achieve:

  • It is not a weight loss tool. Candidates should be at a stable weight before surgery. The procedure removes skin and some fat but is not a substitute for a healthy lifestyle.
  • It does not remove all stretch marks. Only stretch marks located on the skin that is surgically excised (typically below the navel) will be removed. Stretch marks on the upper abdomen or flanks will remain.
  • Results are not entirely permanent without maintenance. Significant future weight gain or pregnancy can stretch the skin and muscles again, altering the results.
  • It leaves a significant scar. There will be a long, permanent scar that extends around the lower torso. While it is placed as low as possible to be concealed by underwear and swimwear, it will always be present.

Discuss Your Contouring Goals with a Specialist Surgeon in London

Making the decision to undergo comprehensive abdominal surgery is a significant step, often marking the final stage of a long journey of weight loss and personal transformation. Understanding the intricacies of the procedure, the recovery process, and the potential outcomes is essential. A private consultation provides the dedicated time and space to explore your concerns and aspirations in a supportive environment.

An expert assessment is necessary to confirm if an extended abdominoplasty is the most appropriate procedure for your unique anatomy and to tailor a surgical plan that aligns with your aesthetic goals. This is your opportunity to ask questions and gain the clarity needed to move forward with confidence.

To discuss your options with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, book a personal consultation at his practice serving patients across London, Hertfordshire, and Stevenage.

Frequently Asked Questions About Extended Tummy Tucks

How much does an extended abdominoplasty cost?

The cost of an extended abdominoplasty is based on an individual's specific surgical requirements. The final fee includes the surgeon's time, anaesthetist fees, and hospital charges. A detailed and precise quotation is provided following your personal consultation with Mr. Roshan Vijayan, once he has assessed your anatomy and discussed your goals.

What are the potential risks of an extended tummy tuck?

As with any significant surgical procedure, an extended tummy tuck carries risks such as infection, bleeding, adverse scarring, and changes in skin sensation. During your consultation, Mr. Vijayan will thoroughly explain all potential complications, ensuring you have a comprehensive understanding to make an informed decision about your care.

When can I return to exercise after the procedure?

Light walking is encouraged shortly after surgery to aid circulation. However, strenuous activities and core exercises must be avoided for at least six to eight weeks to allow the internal muscle repairs to heal properly. Mr. Vijayan will provide a personalised recovery plan and advise when it is safe to resume your specific fitness routine.

How long will the results of an extended abdominoplasty last?

The removal of excess skin and fat provides a long-lasting change to your body's contour. To preserve these results, it is important to maintain a stable weight through a balanced diet and regular exercise. Significant weight fluctuations or future pregnancies can affect the outcome over time.

Is liposuction always performed with an extended abdominoplasty?

Liposuction is frequently combined with an extended abdominoplasty to enhance the final contour. It is particularly useful for reducing stubborn fat deposits on the flanks, hips, and back to create a more defined waistline. Whether it is appropriate for you will be discussed during your surgical planning session.

What is the difference between an extended tummy tuck and a 360 degree tummy tuck?

An extended tummy tuck lengthens the incision around the hips to address the flanks and love handles. A 360 degree tummy tuck, or lower body lift, involves a circumferential incision that continues all the way around the torso to remove excess skin from the back and lift the buttocks as well.
